intro: An inner-product graph decoder turns node embeddings into pairwise edge probabilities. Its geometry imposes symmetry and a particular behavior on self-pairs.
task: Decode every pair of supplied node embeddings with a stable sigmoid. Inspect which graph structures this decoder can express and which assumptions come from the formula itself.
requirements: embeddings is a nonempty real matrix of shape (N,D). Compute scores=embeddings@embeddings.T and return sigmoid(scores) as an (N,N) NumPy array.
Evaluate sigmoid stably for both positive and negative scores. Return probabilities without thresholding, row normalization or removing diagonal entries.
This lesson adapts only the graph autoencoder’s decoder. The embeddings are supplied; no graph convolution encoder, random weights, reconstruction training or negative-edge sampling is included.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Build all pairwise inner products
hints.body: Multiplying embeddings.T@embeddings would compare feature dimensions instead of nodes.

hints.title: Inspect the diagonal
hints.body: A node dotted with itself has nonnegative score. Its returned self-pair probability must therefore be at least one half.

explanation: The score matrix is symmetric, so this decoder cannot independently represent two directions of an edge. Orthogonal node embeddings produce probability one half, not zero.

Every diagonal score is a squared norm. The resulting self-pair probability is at least one half; applications that omit self-edges must handle that in their data or loss rather than silently altering this decoder.

Extracted and ported the upstream graph-autoencoder inner-product decoder to NumPy with stable sigmoid branches. The upstream randomly initialized two-layer encoder is deliberately outside this supplied-embedding contract.
